details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 5 - The Journeymen · Seat 3, Healer

A sharp-tongued hedge-witch who patches the party up and curses whatever is hurting them. Brisk, nosy and kind underneath it; scolds the wounded while she bandages them and talks to her toad more than to people. Mother Loretta says she owes the world a debt; Maud pays it off one rescued fool at a time, and the Keepers find her plenty of fools.

In a fight

Mage Armour every morning; Hex the most dangerous enemy, Sleep packs of goblins, Hold Person their leader, and keep a 2nd-level slot spare for Bind Wound.
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities (from the printed sheet)

Hex (action). Curse one creature within 30ft: Will save (DC 15) or it has Disadvantage on your choice of attack rolls, saves or ability checks for 1 minute (never on saves against the Hex). While hexed it takes 2d6 necrotic at the start of each of its turns and repeats the Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending it on a success. One Hex at a time; a new one ends the old. 3 free Hexes a day (Wis mod), then each costs a 1st-level slot.

Spell Use. Prepare 8 spells each morning from the Witch list (level 5 + Wis 3); 3 cantrips always known. Slots refresh on a long rest. You cannot cast in armour or with a shield.

Familiar: Pudding the toad. 2 HP, AC 14. Acts on its own each round (move, scout, hide, carry small things) and shares what it sees and hears within 1 mile. Speaks a few simple words. If adjacent to a target it can deliver your Hex or a touch spell as your action. Re-bonded after a full rest if killed.

Hag's Vigour. +1 Max HP per Witch level (included).

Patron Buff: Mother Loretta (1/day). Tend a touched creature (or yourself) for 10 minutes: it regains HP as for one night in a safe haven (roll its largest Hit Die and add its Con mod, minimum 0). In combat, instead, as part of your action: it regains 1d8+2 HP.

Human versatility. +1 Wisdom and +1 Constitution (included).

Chosen skill: Perception. Advantage on Wisdom checks to notice things (no NWP slot).

Bonus feat. An extra General feat at 1st level (Will of Iron).

Training. Two extra weapons: light crossbow and short sword. Armour: light, medium (but a Witch still cannot cast in armour).

No darkvision. You need light. Cast Light on your staff.

Will of Iron (General, Human bonus). +2 to Will saves (included) and +1 Wisdom (included).

Toughness (General). +1 Constitution (included), +1 Max HP per level (included), Advantage on Constitution checks.

Expanded Mind (Arcane & Devout). One extra spell slot of your highest available level: a 2nd-level slot (included).

First Aid/Healing (Trained). Advantage to stabilise the dying.

Speed, Initiative and HP. Speed: 30ft · Initiative: +1 · HP: d6: 1st level 6 + Con 3 = 9; levels 2-5: 4 x (4 + 3) = 28; Hag's Vigour +1 per Witch level = +5; Toughness +1 per level = +5. Total 47.

Casting

Every spell is resolved by the target's save against your DC. Tick a slot box when you cast; slots return after a full rest. Cantrips are cast at will. Tick the circle beside a spell to mark it prepared. Prepare 8 spells each morning from the Witch list (level 5 + Wis 3); 3 cantrips always known. You cannot cast in armour or with a shield.

Toll the Dead (cantrip): 60ft, one creature: 2d4 necrotic, or 2d6 if it is already hurt. Will negates.

First Aid (cantrip): Touch: a dying creature is stabilised at its current HP, no roll.

Light (cantrip): Touch an object: bright light 20ft and dim light a further 20ft for 5 hours.

Mage Armour (1st): Touch, a willing creature in no armour: AC 13 + Dex for 8 hours. Cast it on yourself each morning.

Bless (reversible: Bane) (1st): 50ft, up to 6 allies, 1 minute: Advantage on their first attack each round and +1 to saves. Bane: up to 6 enemies get Disadvantage on their first attack each round and -1 to saves; Will negates.

Cure Light Wounds (reversible) (1st): Touch: heal 1d8+5 HP. Reversed: 1d8+5 necrotic, Fortitude halves.

Sleep (1st): 90ft, 15ft radius: roll 2d4+5; that many Levels of creatures fall Unconscious for 1d4 minutes, lowest Level first. Level 5+ creatures, undead and constructs are unaffected. Will negates. Damage wakes them.

Hex of Stumbling (1st): 30ft, one creature: speed halved for 1 minute. Reflex negates. Ideal for running from a troll.

Hold Person (2nd): 120ft, one humanoid: Paralysed for up to 5 rounds; it repeats the Will save at the end of each of its turns. Will negates.

Web (2nd): 60ft, 20ft cube, 50 minutes: creatures are Restrained (Reflex negates on first contact); escaping takes an action and a Strength check vs DC 15. Fire burns it away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 fire to everyone inside (Reflex half).

Bind Wound (2nd): Touch: heal 2d8+5 HP.

Armour Class on the sheet: Mage Armour (cast each morning, 8 hours): 13 + 1 (Dex) + 1 (Ring of Protection) = 15. Without Mage Armour: 10 + 1 + 1 = 12.

Class Abilities

1st Level

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast divine folk-magic spells per the Spells Per Day table. Bonus slots from high Wisdom (see Spellcasting in Arneyan, II).

Familiar

  • Effect: Bond a small animal familiar granted in form by your Patron (a black cat, a raven, a toad, a moth — GM and player agree on the specific creature within the Patron's theme). The familiar has 1 HP per two Witch levels (minimum 1), AC 14, and can deliver a Hex or touch spell on your behalf as your action if adjacent to the target.
  • If the familiar dies, it can be re-bonded after a full rest and a small personal cost the GM determines
  • The familiar can speak a handful of simple words and understands your intent even at a distance within 1 mile
  • At-will, no action cost from you: the familiar acts on its own each round — it can move, scout, hide, or carry small objects independently, sharing what it sees or hears with you at any distance within 1 mile.

Hag's Vigour

  • Effect: Hag-blood runs truer in you than it does in most folk magic practitioners — you're hardier than your spindly d6 Hit Die suggests. Gain a permanent +1 bonus to maximum HP per Witch level.

Hex (Wisdom)

  • Effect: As an action, curse one creature within 30ft — Will save or have Disadvantage on one of: attack rolls, saving throws, or ability checks (your choice when you cast it) for 1 minute. While hexed, it also takes 1d6 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns (2d6 at 5th, 3d6 at 9th, 4d6 at 13th, 5d6 at 17th), and repeats the Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending the Hex on a success. The Disadvantage never applies to saves against the Hex itself. You can have only one Hex active; a new Hex ends the old one. You can Hex for free a number of times per day equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1); each further Hex costs a 1st-level slot.
  • Patron Boon — Buff: gain the 1st-tier Buff granted by your chosen Patron

6th Level

  • Patron Boon — Curse: gain the 1st-tier Curse granted by your chosen Patron

9th Level

Twin Hex

  • Effect: A Hex can also afflict a second creature within 30ft, each with its own save.

12th Level

  • Patron Boon — Physical Change: gain the Physical Change granted by your chosen Patron. It is permanent and visible.

15th Level

  • Patron Boon (Buff) improves: usable twice per day
  • Wisdom Bonus: permanent +1 Wisdom

17th Level

Twin Hex (Improved)

  • Effect: A Hex can afflict a third creature within 30ft, each with its own save.

18th Level

  • Patron Boon (Curse) improves: usable twice per day, and the DC of the target's save increases by 1

20th Level

Cauldron of the Ninth Moon

  • Effect: Once — and only once every several months of in-game time — the Witch may perform the Cauldron ritual. This requires: a full night uninterrupted, a specific lunar or seasonal condition set by the GM, and rare and costly ingredients whose value the GM sets based on the scale of the effect requested.
  • If completed successfully, the ritual produces an effect equivalent to the Wish spell, subject to the same GM discretion and risk of twisted or partial results that Wish carries
  • The Cauldron always leaves a mark on the Witch — a permanent minor cost the GM determines, thematically tied to what was asked for
  • This is not a spell slot or daily resource — it is a story-level event the GM gates behind narrative conditions, not a mechanic to be spammed

24th Level

  • Cauldron of the Ninth Moon improves: the ritual can now be attempted once per month of in-game time rather than requiring the GM's specific rare conditions, though the ingredient cost remains steep
  • Hex improves: it lasts 10 minutes and the first Will save against it is made at Disadvantage

Witch Spells Per Day

  • The Witch draws from a curated folk-magic spell list — a blend of Cleric and Druid spells reflavoured as hedge magic, plus a handful of Patron-specific additions. Bonus spells from high Wisdom apply once the Witch is high enough level to cast that tier. Hexes beyond your free daily uses draw from this same pool of slots — a Witch who spends slots on Hex has fewer left for spells that round, and vice versa.

Witch Spell List

Spells available to the Witch, by level. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue). Full descriptions, saves and components are in Spellcasting in Arneyan. Spells marked in the Class-Only list below exist for this class alone. Includes every Wizard-list spell of the Witch’s favoured schools (Enchantment, Necromancy and Divination), up to the highest spell level the Witch can cast, except Power Word Stun, Power Word Blind and Power Word Kill.

0 Level (Cantrips)

Detect Magic · Detect Poison · First Aid · Ghost Sound · Know Direction · Light · Mending · Purify Food and Drink · Read Magic · Resistance · Toll the Dead

1st Level

Bless* · Charm Person · Chill Touch · Comprehend Languages · Cure Light Wounds* · Entangle · Faerie Fire · Friends · Identify‡ · Mage Armour · Protection from Alignment · Sleep

2nd Level

Augury‡ · Barkskin · Blindness/Deafness · Detect Thoughts* · Hold Person · Invisibility · Locate Object* · Obscuring Mist · Ray of Enfeeblement · See Invisibility · Silence · Speak with Animals · Speak with Dead · Tasha's Hideous Laughter · Web

Class-Only Spells

Ill Omen (Cantrip) — Range 30ft; one creature has Disadvantage on its next check within the hour; Will negates.

Hex of Stumbling (1st) — Range 30ft; one creature's speed is halved for 1 minute; Reflex negates.

Bind Wound (2nd) — Touch; heals 2d8 HP plus 1 per level (max +10).

Evil Eye (2nd) — Range 30ft; one creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 minute; Will negates, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.

Contagion (3rd) — Touch; one creature catches a disease of your choice (see Disease & Poison in The Arneyan Codex), with effects starting at once; Fortitude negates.

Withering Glance (3rd) — Range 30ft; one creature ages 1d4 years (the ageing is permanent) and has −1 Strength and Constitution for 1 day; Fortitude negates.

Wither Limb (4th) — Range 30ft; one limb of a creature is useless for 1 day per level (an arm drops what it holds; a leg halves speed); Fortitude negates. Remove Curse or Restoration ends it.

Withering Curse (8th) — Range 30ft; one creature takes 1 Constitution damage at the start of each of its turns; Fortitude negates, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on a success. Remove Curse also ends it. Lost Constitution returns at 1 point per full rest once the curse ends.

Patrons

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Witch folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose one Patron at character creation. Your Patron defines your familiar's form, your spell list's flavour, and the specific Buff (1st), Curse (6th), and Physical Change (12th) you receive. Five of Arneyan's classic hag types are represented here, alongside the folkloric Baba Yaga and two wholly original Arneyan patrons.
  • Patron — Vashtira, the Widow of Dreams (Night Hag)
  • She walks the space between sleep and waking, riding the dreams of the exhausted and collecting what they'd rather forget. Her Witches wake tired for reasons they can't explain, carrying a little less of themselves than they went to bed with.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) advantage on saves vs fear and mind-affecting effects for 1 hour — the recipient sleeps a little less easily afterward.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, afflict a creature within 30ft with Vashtira's Weight (Will save against your Class Save DC) — while cursed, the target's dreams are haunted and they gain no benefit from rest until the curse is lifted or a week passes.
  • Physical Change (12th): Your eyes lose their whites — solid black, cold to look into. You gain darkvision and advantage on saves vs being magically put to sleep. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day, without spending your action, lock your gaze on a creature within 30ft — Will save or frightened for 1 round and shaken (disadvantage on their next attack roll) for 1 minute after.
  • Patron — Old Mossmaw of the Nalwood Deep (Green Hag)
  • Every swamp has one, or claims to. Old Mossmaw wears a different lovely face every time she's seen, and every villager who's traded with her swears they got the better deal — until they check what they actually walked away with.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) a glamour — +4 to Deception and Persuasion checks for 1 hour, appearance unchanged to true sight or careful magical scrutiny. While the glamour lasts, the first attack made against the recipient in each encounter has Disadvantage.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to see themselves as hideous in every reflective surface for 24 hours (Will save negates) — disadvantage on Charisma checks with anyone who has seen their reflection.
  • Physical Change (12th): Your skin takes on a faint mottled green cast in dim light, and warts bloom at your knuckles. Advantage on Stealth checks in swamp, marsh, or bog terrain. Your hands harden with a bog-witch's grip — unarmed strikes deal 1d6 damage and you gain advantage on grapple and overbearing checks.
  • Patron — Grigsdotter Ironjaw (Annis Hag)
  • A hill-den brute with a grip that's cracked stone and a temper to match. Grigsdotter doesn't bargain in riddles like the others — she bargains in favours owed and debts collected, and she always collects.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) advantage on Strength checks and +1d6 damage on their next successful melee hit within 1 minute.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, mark a creature within 30ft — your next successful Hex against them deals an additional 2d6 damage (Fortitude save halves).
  • Physical Change (12th): Your nails thicken into short, blackened claws. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage, and gain advantage on Strength checks to break or force objects. If you strike the same target with both a claw attack and a successful Hex in the same round, the claw deals an additional 1d6 damage.
  • Patron — The Drowned Widow of Coldmere Bay (Sea Hag)
  • Fishermen along the Jinia coast leave offerings at low tide so she doesn't come looking herself. She was beautiful once, or so the stories insist, right before the sea decided otherwise.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) a swim speed equal to their normal move speed and the ability to hold their breath for 1 hour. Their first melee hit within that hour also forces a Fortitude save or the target is knocked prone, coughing seawater.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to make a Will save or be wracked by the Drowned Widow's Gaze — disadvantage on all rolls for 1 minute as the ocean's weight presses on their mind.
  • Physical Change (12th): Your skin turns faintly grey and clammy, and thin gill-like slits appear at your throat. You can breathe underwater and gain a swim speed of 20ft. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day, make a melee touch attack instead — the target makes a Fortitude save or their lungs seize with phantom water, staggered (half speed, disadvantage on attack rolls) for 1 minute.
  • Patron — Frostmother Ysolde (Bheur Hag)
  • She comes down from the high passes when the first real cold sets in, and the old villages of the Boldock Wall still leave out food so she passes them by. Some winters she doesn't take the offering. Those are the bad years.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) immunity to natural cold and exhaustion from harsh weather for 24 hours. For the first minute, any creature that hits them in melee takes 1d6 cold damage.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to make a Fortitude save or their speed is halved by bone-deep cold for 1 minute, taking 1d6 cold damage at the start of each of their turns while affected.
  • Physical Change (12th): Frost rimes your hair permanently white regardless of true age, and your breath mists even in warm air. Resistance 5 to cold damage. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per round when you hit with a Hex, a damaging spell, or this claw attack, you may add 1d6 cold damage to the effect, no additional cost.
  • Patron — Baba Yaga
  • The Grandmother of Witches, older than any coven that claims her, older than most of the borders on any map of Arneyan. Her hut walks on chicken legs somewhere out past the edge of settled land, and it finds the Witches it wants to find — not the other way around.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) advantage on all Wisdom and Intelligence-based checks for one hour — Baba Yaga's wisdom lends itself, briefly, to those she favours. They also have Advantage on their next Will save within the hour.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, set a creature within 30ft an impossible task as a curse (Will save negates) — on a failed save they immediately suffer disadvantage on all Charisma checks until they attempt the task in good faith (for up to 1 day per Witch level), as if the world itself is waiting on them to finish.
  • Physical Change (12th): Your teeth sharpen slightly and one lock of your hair turns iron-grey no matter your true age. Advantage on Survival checks in deep wilderness, and you always know which direction leads to the nearest dwelling, however far. You may make an unarmed bite attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day as a reaction when struck in melee, the ancient magic in your blood answers unbidden — the attacker makes a Will save or suffers disadvantage on their next attack roll.
  • Patron — Mother Loretta
  • Ancient beyond any coven's memory of her arrival, Mother Loretta is said to have written down half the hexes every Witch in Arneyan still uses — usually without anyone crediting her for it. She doesn't take students anymore. She just occasionally shows up to collect what she considers owed.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, tend a touched creature (or yourself) for 10 minutes: they regain HP as for one night of rest in a safe haven. No slot recovery. In combat you may instead tend them as part of your action: they regain 1d8 HP plus 1 per two Witch levels.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, unravel a piece of luck from a creature within 30ft — their next d20 roll within 1 hour is rolled twice, worst result used (Will save negates).
  • Physical Change (12th): Your hair greys prematurely regardless of true age, and small green shoots occasionally bud at your temples. Advantage on Wisdom checks involving herbalism, folk remedies, or oral tradition. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day, spit a hex-laced tonic at a creature within 15ft as an action instead — Fortitude save or poisoned (disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks) for 1 minute.
  • Patron — The Hollow Bride
  • A Mournas legend — a bride who drowned in the harbour on her wedding night and never stopped waiting at the water's edge. Witches who serve her carry a little of that patience, and a little of that grief.
  • Buff (1st): Once per day, grant a touched creature (or yourself) immunity to being tracked or scried upon for 1 hour — the Hollow Bride hides what is hers. In the first round of any fight within that hour, attacks against them have Disadvantage.
  • Curse (6th): Once per day, bind a creature within 30ft to a single spoken promise (Will save negates) — if they knowingly break it within 24 hours, they take 3d6 cold damage and know exactly why.
  • Physical Change (12th): Your skin is faintly cool to the touch and you no longer cast a reflection in still water. Advantage on Swim checks and on saves vs drowning or exhaustion in water. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day, make a melee touch attack instead — on a hit, the target takes 2d6 cold damage and must hold their breath or gain one level of exhaustion, as the harbour water fills their lungs for a moment too long.

activities.name: Tend in combat
activities.text: As part of your action: a touched creature (or you) regains 1d8 HP plus 1 per two Witch levels.

activities.name: Tend for 10 minutes
activities.text: The touched creature regains HP as for one night of rest in a safe haven. No slot recovery.

features.name: Patron Curse
features.description: Once per day, unravel a piece of luck from a creature within 30ft — their next d20 roll within 1 hour is rolled twice, worst result used (Will save negates).

features.name: Physical Change
features.description: Your hair greys prematurely regardless of true age, and small green shoots occasionally bud at your temples. Advantage on Wisdom checks involving herbalism, folk remedies, or oral tradition. You may make an unarmed claw attack dealing 1d6 damage. Once per day, spit a hex-laced tonic at a creature within 15ft as an action instead — Fortitude save or poisoned (disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks) for 1 minute.

activities.name: Claw (1d6)
activities.text: An unarmed claw attack (the Unarmed Strike action) dealing this on a hit.

activities.name: Hex-laced tonic
activities.text: Once per day, as an action instead: a creature within 15ft makes a Fortitude save or is Poisoned (Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks) for 1 minute.

system.description:
(Wisdom / Intelligence / Charisma — choose one for the stat bump)

Permanent +2 bonus to Will saving throws. Gain +1 to one of Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma of your choice (once, on taking this feat).

Open to all classes by default.

(Constitution) Gain +1 Max HP per level (retroactive). Gain +1 to Constitution (once, on taking this feat). Advantage on Constitution-based checks.

Open to all classes by default.

You gain one additional spell slot of your highest currently available spell level.

Available to: Wizards, Clerics, Druids, Illusionists, Paladins, Magi, Bards, Sorcerers, Warlocks, Witches, Necromancers, and Artificers.

Touch; one dying creature is stabilised at its current HP (no roll). It stays Unconscious until healed or until 1 hour passes. Restores no HP.

Classes: Illusionist, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Witch

Touch; one object; 1 hour per level. The object sheds bright light in a 20ft radius and dim light for another 20ft.

Classes: Wizard, Illusionist, Cleric, Druid, Warlock, Sorcerer, Bard, Paladin, Magus, Witch

Touch; one willing creature wearing no armour; 8 hours. An unseen field of force surrounds the target, giving AC 13 + Dexterity modifier. It counts as armour only for features and items that require wearing no armour; it never affects casting. The spell ends if the target puts on armour or if you cast it again.

Classes: Wizard, Illusionist, Necromancer, Sorcerer, Magus, Witch, Bard

Range 50ft; up to 6 allies; 1 minute. Targets have Advantage on their first attack roll each round and gain +1 to saving throws. Cast reversed (Bane): up to 6 enemies within range have Disadvantage on their first attack roll each round and suffer -1 to saving throws for 1 minute; Will negates.

Reversible: may be cast as its opposite with the same slot.

Classes: Cleric, Paladin, Witch

Range 90ft; 15ft radius. Creatures with a total of 2d4 Levels + CL fall Unconscious for 1d4 minutes (lowest Level first; creatures of Level 5 or higher unaffected); damage wakes a sleeper. Will negates. Undead and constructs are immune.
